messages:
maya-docs: Quick thread \u2014 opened PR to add a short 'Provisioning gotchas' section for Dedicated (private) with terraform + python SDK examples. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/1620. Can infra and QA skim?
owen-tf: will look. Can you include a tiny example showing GPU nodeSelector + taints for private clusters? Lots of infra teams ask.
maya-docs: added a k8s snippet and an HCL example that shows node_selector + tolerations + reserved_pool_ref mapping. snippet:
```yaml
# k8s pod template for Dedicated private runtime
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator: nvidia-t4
  tolerations:
  - key: \"redwood.gpu\"
    operator: Exists
    effect: NoSchedule
  annotations:
    redwood.ai/tenant-affinity: \"team-ops\"
```
```hcl
resource "redwood_scale_policy" "gpu_tenant" {
  name = "gpu-tenant-ops"
  min_replicas = 1
  max_replicas = 4
  cooldown_ms = 120000
  metrics {
    type = "RequestRate"
    target = 180
  }
  reserved_pool_ref = "teams/ops/gpu-reserved"
  labels = { \"redwood.tenant.isolation\" = \"team-ops\" }
}
```
rachel-qa: useful. please add a QA step to repro an eviction scenario: run high memory load and check for soft-evict log entry `eviction_soft_triggered` and metric `redwood_evictions_total`. I'll add curl commands.
noah-eng: small runtime compatibility note: we accept the HCL field `reserved_pool_ref` and the API expects namespaced form `teams/ops/gpu-reserved`. Also the runtime will prefer `RequestRate` for metrics.type; QPS and RPS are legacy aliases for one release.
maya-docs: added QA commands and the eviction check. Also included a short paragraph clarifying billing language: using reserved pools routes workload to committed capacity; phrased as \"expected billing behavior\" per legal.
owen-tf: nit: in terraform provider v0.13 older attribute `cooldown_seconds` still works but is deprecated; add a conversion note and a tiny snippet showing cooldown_ms.
maya-docs: done, I included a short mapping table: cooldown_seconds -> cooldown_ms (multiply by 1000), pool_id -> reserved_pool_ref (namespaced).
eng-runtime-bot: FYI: compatibility window: aliases accepted for one release. When reserved_pool_ref points to non-existent pool we return 409 reserved_pool_conflict. If capacity tight, servers emit `capacity_unavailable_preemption_possible`. Add both to troubleshooting.
rachel-qa: added a smoke test checklist: create reserved pool, apply scale policy, ramp traffic, verify RPS target hit, check that in-flight requests complete on preemption and error codes are 503 for preempted requests. I can paste test scripts.
maya-docs: added the QA scripts and fixed two broken anchors discovered by linkcheck. Also added a tiny python SDK snippet demonstrating create API:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(token=REDACTED)
client.scale_policies.create({
  \"name\": \"gpu-tenant-ops\",
  \"min_replicas\": 1,
  \"max_replicas\": 4,
  \"cooldown_ms\": 120000,
  \"metrics\": [{\"type\":\"RequestRate\",\"target\":180}],
  \"labels\": {\"redwood.tenant.isolation\":\"team-ops\"},
  \"reserved_pool_ref\": \"teams/ops/gpu-reserved\"
})
```
nowen-tf: LGTM. minor HCL formatting nit left on PR.
devx-bot: Preview deployed: https://deploys.redwood.com/preview/1620 (expires in 7 days). CI: lint OK.
maya-docs: thanks all \u2014 I'll merge after the tf nit and a final eng-runtime ack. Appreciate the quick reviews! :tada:
